objective.value: Develop phage-resistant Escherichia coli host strains for laboratory and industrial bioprocesses by simultaneous genomic integration of the DNA phosphorothioation-based SspBCDE defense module and mutation of host components essential for phage infection cycles, while preserving growth and recombinant protein production capability.
objective.notes: Stated in abstract and Introduction ('In this work, we choose the E. coli MG1655, MG1655 (DE3), and W3110 strains... with the objective of constructing E. coli host strains with broad antiphage activities').

hypothesis.value: Combining a sequence-independent PT-modification-based restriction barrier (SspBCDE, which is non-toxic to hosts lacking sspABCD) with removal/mutation of phage-essential host factors (FhuA receptor loop 8 for T1/T5/phi80; TrxA processivity factor for T7) will confer broader and stronger phage resistance than either mechanism alone, without impairing cell growth or recombinant protein production.

inference.method: synthesis of explicit design rationale statements across Introduction and Results
inference.rationale: Paper states SspBCDE alone did not protect against T5 (results_p001, EOP data) and that 'To achieve a sufficient level of tolerance to phages T5 and T7, the elements in the MG1655-PT strain that are essential to the infection cycle of these phages were modified' (results_p004/p006); Introduction states SspE is non-toxic unlike R-M systems (p005). The combined-strategy hypothesis is implied by the 3-step design and Fig. 5 schematic but is not stated verbatim as a formal hypothesis.

hypothesis.notes: No explicit 'we hypothesize' statement; hypothesis reconstructed from design logic.

value.MG1655-PT: int(aslA-glmZ)::sspBCD (two-step double crossover at SS9 via pKOV-Kan vector pWHU6401) plus sspE integrated by lambda-red recombineering (FRT-flanked Kan cassette from pKD13, removed with pCP20); confirmed by genome sequencing
value.MG1655-EPR: MG1655-PT + fhuA(Delta552-558 NSEG) [deletion of residues 552-558 encoding extracellular loop 8, with NESG/NSEG peptide inserted to preserve beta-barrel formation] + Delta trxA; both via pKOV-Kan two-step double-crossover (pWHU6402, pWHU6403)
value.W3110-PT / W3110-EPR: same engineering scheme in W3110 background (Supplementary Fig. 5)
value.MG1655(DE3)-PT / MG1655(DE3)-EPR: same engineering scheme in MG1655(DE3) background (Supplementary Fig. 5)

engineering_method.value: Three-step genome engineering strategy: (1) chromosomal integration of the sspBCD cluster at safe site SS9 (aslA-glmZ intergenic region) using pKOV-Kan two-step double-crossover gene replacement; (2) lambda Red-mediated recombineering to integrate sspE adjacent to sspBCD, FRT/Kan marker removal with pCP20 FLP recombinase, plasmid curing at 42 C, verification by colony PCR and genome sequencing; (3) sequential two-step double-crossover mutations deleting FhuA extracellular loop 8 (fhuA Delta552-558 with NESG peptide insertion) and deleting trxA. Prior plasmid-based validation used pWHU3640 (Gibson assembly into pBluescript II SK(+)).
engineering_method.notes: Discussion describes this as a '3-step feasible strategy'. Intermediate strain naming: E. coli int(aslA-glmZ)::sspBCD then E. coli-PT then E. coli-EPR.

analysis_methods.value: Fold protection computed as EOP on sspBCDE-containing strain divided by EOP on empty-vector/parent strain; growth-curve comparison of OD600 trajectories; one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's test for flask production data; DAAO activity from pyruvate calibration curve (20-500 uM, DNP derivatization, A445); soluble nsp8 concentration by Bradford assay with BSA standard after SDS-PAGE confirmation; sspE/sspBCD expression ratio by RT-qPCR; genomic integrity assessed by LM-PCR banding patterns and genome sequencing of integration mutants.
analysis_methods.notes: Statistical treatment only explicitly reported for Fig. 4b-d (ANOVA + Tukey); no statistics described for EOP fold protection.

value.sspBCDE_plasmid: Conferred PT modification, no growth defect, up to 10^6-fold EOP protection against most coliphages; T5 insensitive (attributed to two-step DNA injection); effective across MG1655, MG1655(DE3), W3110, BW25113, JM109, OP50 and E. coli W
value.PT_strains: Chromosomal sspBCDE integration gave same growth as plasmid version, slightly higher sspE:sspBCD expression ratio, and at least 10-fold increased protection against T1, T4, EEP and lambda vs plasmid system
value.EPR_strains: Extremely strong resistance to all tested coliphages (plaques barely formed at highest titer); no lysis at MOI 10 for T1/T5/EEP/JMPW2; significant resistance to T4/T7 at MOI 0.1 and lambda at MOI 0.5; growth identical to parents
value.protein_production_flask: Under phage cocktail, MG1655-EPR and W3110-EPR (pGEMKT-DAAO) reached OD600 ~5.3 and 4.8 at 12 h with DAAO activities 2.03 +/- 0.07 and 1.88 +/- 0.10 U/mL (comparable to unchallenged parents); MG1655(DE3)-EPR (pWHU6404) produced ~64 mg/L soluble nsp8 under cocktail challenge
value.fed_batch: MG1655-EPR(pGEMKT-DAAO) maintained 28.53 +/- 2.79 U/mL DAAO with cocktail (vs ~0 for challenged WT; 27.76 +/- 0.75 without); W3110-EPR 28.44 +/- 2.27 U/mL with cocktail; nsp8 expression 1.52/1.58/1.46 g/L for WT-no-phage, EPR-no-phage, EPR-with-phage respectively; DO profiles similar to uninfected parents
value.stability: Phage resistance and production maintained over 47 transfers (~400 generations); no escape phages emerged in 48 h fermentations; no genomic changes detectable by LM-PCR

outcomes.notes: 'Strong resistance to all tested phages' is scoped to the 7 coliphages tested (T1, JMPW2, T5, lambda, EEP, T4, T7) and to MOIs/durations examined; authors explicitly decline to generalize to all E. coli backgrounds or other species (discussion_p021). Long-term phage escape evolution tested only via 400-generation host serial transfer and 48 h fermentations; no directed phage-evolution/escape assay.

experimental_design_object.title: Systematic strategies for developing phage resistant Escherichia coli strains

experiments.purpose: Validate that plasmid-borne SspBCDE from E. coli 3234/A confers DNA PT modification and broad phage protection in laboratory/industrial E. coli hosts without growth cost
experiments.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (primary); extended to MG1655(DE3), W3110, BW25113, JM109, E. coli B OP50, wild-type E. coli W
experiments.intervention: Transformation with pWHU3640 (pBluescript II SK(+) carrying ~8 kb sspBCDE cassette cloned from E. coli 3234/A genomic DNA via PCR + Gibson assembly)
experiments.conditions: LB, 37 C, 100 ug/mL ampicillin; phage challenge at MOI 0.05/0.5/5 at OD600 0.6 (growth curves, 12 h) or t=0 per Fig. 1c caption; plaque spot assay 12 h; EOP overnight
experiments.control: Same hosts with empty vector pBluescript II SK(+); LB blank reference
experiments.replicates: three independent experiments (mean +/- SD); plaque morphology assay repeated at least three times
experiments.readout: OD600 growth curves, plaque size/morphology, EOP fold protection
experiments.analysis: EOP ratio pWHU3640-host / empty-vector-host; descriptive comparison of growth curves
experiments.outcome: Up to 10^6-fold protection against most tested coliphages; no protection against T5; no growth impairment; protection observed across all 7 host backgrounds

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass: authors actively cloned the sspBCDE cassette and constructed pWHU3640 transformants. Q2 pass: cloning and host introduction performed in this study (system identified in their earlier work, but this construct and these host introductions are new). Q3 pass: results (broad protection except T5, plus plasmid-system limitations) directly motivated the subsequent genome-integration and host-factor-mutation decisions.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Introducing a heterologous defense system relieves the host's intrinsic susceptibility to phage DNA replication; closest controlled category is 'derepression of a limiting/relief mechanism' (M3 解除调控) in the sense of adding a defensive barrier, though the vocabulary does not map perfectly to antiphage defense.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: The SspABCD-SspE system was recently identified by the group as a PT-modulated defense system with broad antiphage activity and no toxicity to hosts lacking sspABCD, making it a candidate module for host protection (p005); plasmid delivery chosen as the quick evaluation route before genome integration.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Outcome measured directly by EOP, plaque assays and growth curves.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Choice of module rests on the group's prior published characterization of SspABCD-SspE (ref 30) and its established non-toxicity relative to R-M systems; no new mechanistic derivation in this paper drove the choice.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When engineering phage resistance into phage-sensitive E. coli production hosts, first evaluate the candidate defense module on a plasmid across multiple host backgrounds and a phage panel spanning all three Caudovirales morphological families, because module efficacy is host- and phage-dependent and plasmid delivery allows rapid screening before committing to genome integration.
alternatives_considered: Plasmid-encoded natural antiphage systems previously used in dairy starter strains (CRISPR-Cas, Abi, antisense mRNA, R-M) noted as background approaches with narrow range or postsegregational killing risk
R-M systems rejected implicitly because REase loss causes host cell death; SspE chosen because it is non-toxic without sspABCD

experiments.purpose: Generate stable phage-resistant strain avoiding plasmid incompatibility, instability, copy-number variation and metabolic burden
experiments.intervention: Integration of 5.4 kb sspBCD at safe site SS9 (int(aslA-glmZ)) via pKOV-Kan two-step double crossover (pWHU6401); subsequent lambda-red recombineering integration of 2.6 kb sspE with FRT-Kan marker (pKD46 induced with 0.2% arabinose; pKD13 template), marker excision with pCP20, plasmid curing at 42 C, verification by colony PCR and genome sequencing -> E. coli-PT strains
experiments.conditions: LB, 37 C; kanamycin 50 ug/mL selection; overnight 42 C curing
experiments.control: MG1655 parent and MG1655(pWHU3640) for growth and expression comparison
experiments.replicates: unknown for construction; phenotypic EOP comparisons at least three independent experiments (Fig. 2d)
experiments.readout: Colony PCR, genome sequencing, growth profile, RT-qPCR sspE:sspBCD ratio, EOP
experiments.analysis: Comparison of expression ratio and fold protection vs plasmid-borne module
experiments.outcome: MG1655-PT grows like MG1655(pWHU3640); sspE:sspBCD ratio slightly higher; at least 10-fold increased protection against T1, T4, EEP, lambda vs plasmid system

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass: deliberate chromosomal integration of sspBCDE. Q2 pass: performed in this study. Q3 pass: established the -PT platform from which fhuA/trxA mutations and the three EPR strains were derived, and demonstrated improved protection vs plasmid, confirming genome integration as the strategy backbone.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Stable genomic installation of the defense barrier to permanently relieve phage susceptibility (defense-module installation; nearest category M3).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Plasmid-encoded defense is limited by plasmid incompatibility, instability, copy-number variability and metabolic burden of plasmid maintenance (results_p002, citing refs 36, 37).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Integration verified by colony PCR and genome sequencing; protection gain measured by EOP.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: SS9 chosen because published work (ref 40, Bassalo et al.) identified it as an intergenic safe site with high integration efficiency and expression without viability cost; rationale adopted from literature rather than newly derived mechanistically in this paper.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When converting a plasmid-borne defense or pathway module into a stable industrial E. coli host, integrate the module at a characterized intergenic safe site (e.g., SS9) using markerless two-step double-crossover plus lambda-red recombineering, because chromosomal integration removes plasmid-instability and antibiotic-selection burdens while preserving host viability.
alternatives_considered: Continued use of plasmid-borne sspBCDE (rejected due to plasmid incompatibility/instability/copy-number/metabolic burden)

experiments.purpose: Achieve tolerance to phages T5 and T7, which evaded or were insufficiently restricted by SspBCDE alone
experiments.intervention: Deletion of FhuA extracellular loop 8 (fhuA Delta552-558 with NESG peptide insertion to preserve beta-barrel formation) via pWHU6402 two-step double crossover, followed by trxA deletion via pWHU6403 -> E. coli-EPR strains
experiments.conditions: LB, 37 C; sequential construction; verification by genome sequencing
experiments.control: WT, plasmid-bearing and -PT counterparts in each background
experiments.replicates: plaque assays representative of three independent experiments; EOP data at least three times
experiments.readout: Plaque assay, EOP, growth curves at MOI up to 10, phage cocktail challenge
experiments.analysis: Qualitative plaque formation and quantitative EOP/growth-curve comparison across the four genotypes per background
experiments.outcome: Plaques barely formed on EPR lawns even at highest phage titer; no lysis by T1/T5/EEP/JMPW2 at MOI 10; significant resistance to T4/T7 at MOI 0.1 and lambda at MOI 0.5; identical growth to parents; resistant to 7-phage cocktail

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass: targeted genomic deletions of fhuA loop 8 and trxA. Q2 pass: constructed in this study. Q3 pass: produced the final EPR chassis used for all production demonstrations and defined the paper's 3-step strategy.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Blocking phage infection routes by removing the host receptor determinant (FhuA loop 8 for T1/T5/phi80) and an essential host factor (TrxA processivity factor for T7 DNA polymerase) - functional analogue of removing competing/enabling pathway elements (M5 竞争/旁路通量阻断).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: EOP data showed phage T5 was insensitive to SspBCDE defense (results_p001) and T7 remained a threat; known biology: T1/T5/phi80 use FhuA as receptor (ref 41) and T7 uses host TrxA as processivity factor (ref 42).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Insensitivity of T5 measured by EOP (hard data); receptor/factor roles grounded in cited experimental literature; outcome verified by plaque/EOP/growth assays.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Choice of fhuA loop 8 and trxA is directly based on published identification of FhuA as the T1/T5/phi80 receptor and TrxA as the T7 polymerase processivity factor; the paper cites these studies rather than deriving the targets de novo. Mechanistic logic (receptor removal blocks adsorption/injection) underlies it, so both tags apply.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a DNA-level defense system leaves specific phages unrestricted in an E. coli production host, layer receptor/essential-host-factor mutations targeting those phages' infection cycle (e.g., delete FhuA loop 8 for FhuA-dependent phages, delete trxA for T7-family polymerase dependence) on top of the defense module, because phages unable to inject or replicate DNA cannot escape through restriction-insensitivity mechanisms.

experiments.purpose: Test whether EPR strains maintain recombinant protein production under high-titer phage cocktail challenge
experiments.host: MG1655-EPR and W3110-EPR carrying pGEMKT-DAAO; MG1655(DE3)-EPR carrying pWHU6404
experiments.intervention: Transformation of production plasmids (constitutive dao from Trigonopsis variabilis; IPTG-inducible T7-driven nsp8) into EPR strains; phage cocktail added at start of cultivation
experiments.conditions: 2 L baffled flasks, 1 L LB, 37 C; DAAO 12 h; nsp8 induced 0.1 mM IPTG at OD600 0.6 then 28 C for 18 h; cocktail: 4.0x10^9 PFU/L T4+T7, 2.0x10^10 PFU/L lambda, 4.0x10^11 PFU/L T1/JMPW2/T5/EEP
experiments.control: SM-buffer blank (no phage) for each strain/plasmid; WT parents with plasmid +/- cocktail
experiments.readout: OD600, DAAO activity (U/mL), soluble nsp8 concentration (SDS-PAGE + Bradford)
experiments.analysis: One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's test
experiments.outcome: EPR strains grew robustly and produced DAAO (2.03 +/- 0.07 and 1.88 +/- 0.10 U/mL) and nsp8 (~64 mg/L) under cocktail challenge, comparable to unchallenged parents; WT controls died under cocktail

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails for the production test itself: no new engineering action is introduced here - already-constructed EPR strains are transformed with standard expression plasmids and benchmarked; it validates the prior engineering decisions without generating a new design choice.

experiments.purpose: Assess EPR strain robustness during fed-batch fermentation, the industrial mode most vulnerable to phage attack
experiments.host: MG1655-EPR(pGEMKT-DAAO), W3110-EPR(pGEMKT-DAAO), MG1655(DE3)-EPR(pWHU6404) with WT counterparts
experiments.intervention: Fed-batch cultivation in 5 L bioreactor with high-concentration phage cocktail added at start; IPTG (1 mM) induction at OD600 20 with 28 C shift for nsp8
experiments.conditions: 1.9 L initial medium (20 g/L tryptone, 14 g/L yeast extract, 10 g/L NaCl, 20 g/L glycerol); pH 7.5 (5 M NaOH); 4 L/min air; 400-600 rpm; feed 200 g/L glycerol + 40 g/L tryptone + 20 g/L yeast extract; 48 h; cocktail 5.0x10^9 PFU/L T4+T7, 2.5x10^10 PFU/L lambda, 5.0x10^11 PFU/L T1/JMPW2/T5/EEP
experiments.control: SM-buffer/no-phage fermentation of each strain; WT + cocktail groups
experiments.readout: OD600, DO profiles, DAAO activity, nsp8 titer
experiments.outcome: EPR strains matched unchallenged growth/DO profiles; DAAO 28.53 +/- 2.79 U/mL (MG1655-EPR + cocktail) vs ~0 for challenged WT; nsp8 1.46 +/- 0.09 g/L with cocktail vs 1.52 +/- 0.16 for WT without; no phage escape observed over 48 h

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: no new genetic or process engineering decision - the fixed EPR chassis and standard fed-batch operation are benchmarked against phage challenge; results confirm the strategy rather than drive a new modification.

experiments.purpose: Determine inheritance of phage resistance and fermentation stability of EPR strains over long-term propagation
experiments.intervention: Serial transfer every 12 h at 1:1000 dilution for 47 transfers (~400 generations) at 37 C; periodic phenotyping
experiments.conditions: LB, 37 C; sampling every 20 generations (shake-flask fermentation) and every 40 generations (plaque assay)
experiments.control: none beyond initial-generation baseline (no separate control strain described)
experiments.readout: Plaque assay (resistance), shake-flask fermentation performance; LM-PCR for genomic integrity
experiments.outcome: Resistance and production maintained through ~400 generations; no genomic changes detected by LM-PCR even after phage-cocktail exposure

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: serial passaging here is a stability measurement campaign, not a deliberate engineering modification or selection campaign intended to create a new trait; it characterizes the already-built strains.

experimental_design_object.causal_chain: Plasmid validation (EXP1) identified SspBCDE breadth and the T5 gap -> genome integration (EXP2) removed plasmid liabilities and improved protection -> host-factor mutation (EXP3) closed T5/T7 gaps yielding EPR chassis -> flask (EXP4), fed-batch (EXP5) and 400-generation stability (EXP6) validated industrial applicability.

article_type_gate.rationale: Abstract reports new engineered strains and experiments; Results describe original strain construction and assays; Methods detail protocols; author contributions confirm experiments conducted by the authors. Nature Communications original research article.

engineering_paper_type.engineering_paper_type_rationale: The paper's main contribution is redesigning E. coli host chassis for robustness (phage resistance) via genomic integration of a defense module plus host-factor deletions; it is not a metabolite-production, biosensor, evolution, or enzyme-variant study. Application demonstrations use recombinant protein production as a readout of chassis quality.

conflicts.topic: Inserted peptide sequence in fhuA loop-8 deletion construct
conflicts.prose_interpretation: methods_p006 heading reads 'Construction of fhuA(Delta552-558 NSEG)' while the body sentence reads 'The peptide NESG was inserted into the deletion region to prevent structural restrictions in beta-barrel formation' - the four residues are ordered differently (NSEG vs NESG).
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: No figure resolves the residue order; likely a typographical inconsistency or OCR artifact, but cannot be disambiguated from available text.
conflicts.impact: Exact reconstruction of the fhuA mutant allele requires the intended peptide order; low functional impact expected (same four residues) but sequence-accurate strain rebuilding is blocked pending resolution.

conflicts.topic: OD600 threshold for IPTG induction of nsp8 in flask culture
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Results (results_p010) state induction when OD600 reached 0.6-0.8 with 0.1 mM IPTG.
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Methods (methods_p015) state IPTG added when OD600 reached 0.6.
conflicts.impact: Minor procedural discrepancy (0.6 vs 0.6-0.8); exact protocol reproduction should note the range.

conflicts.topic: Timing of phage addition in Fig. 1c growth-curve experiment
conflicts.prose_interpretation: Methods (methods_p009) state phages were added when culture OD600 reached 0.6.
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Fig. 1c caption (results_p005) states 'Bacteria were infected at t = 0 at MOIs of 5, 0.5 and 0.05'.
conflicts.impact: Different infection timing for the microplate growth-curve assay; reproduction requires choosing one - flag for manual review; possibly two variants of the assay (Fig. 1c vs Fig. 3a).

conflicts.prose_interpretation: Fig. 4 caption (discussion_p015): 'means of duplicate fermentation profiles' - replicate type (independent fermenter runs vs technical) not defined; flask experiments use 'three biological replicates' while Fig. 1-3 use 'three independent experiments'.
conflicts.impact: Statistical strength of fed-batch conclusions uncertain; replicate classification remains 'unresolved'.

conflicts.prose_interpretation: Several values contain OCR noise, e.g., '2.0 x 10^10' rendered with stray diacritics in results_p009/methods_p016, '2.03 +/- 0.07' as '$2 . 0 3 \pm 0 . 0 { \bar { 7 } }$', and '27.65 +/- 2.89' partially garbled in results_p011.
conflicts.equation_or_figure_interpretation: Values interpreted by context; readings recorded in outcomes field.
conflicts.impact: Low risk of misread digits; recommend verification against Source Data for exact values.
